key_insight: A PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-Si trilayer improves solar-cell efficiency while using graphene to protect the junction against environmental degradation.
engineering_relevance: The planar architecture combines optical, electrical, and protective functions to improve the performance and durability of hybrid silicon photovoltaics.
method: Fabricate PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-Si junctions on untextured silicon.
Benchmark against graphene/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si reference cells.
Assess optoelectronic behavior and efficiency retention over 75 days in ambient conditions.
evidence_signal: The trilayer achieved 8.52% efficiency versus 4.56% for graphene/n-Si and retained approximately 90% of its initial efficiency after 75 days, versus approximately 29% for PEDOT:PSS/n-Si.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish durability beyond 75 days or the scalability of producing defect-free graphene barriers.
paper_title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells
